records.source: כֹּ֤ה הִרְאַ֨נִי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִנֵּה֙ יוֹצֵ֣ר גֹּבַ֔י בִּתְחִלַּ֖ת עֲל֣וֹת הַלָּ֑קֶשׁ וְהִ֨נֵּה־לֶ֔קֶשׁ אַחַ֖ר גִּזֵּ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: Thus showed me [the] Lord Yahweh, and look, he [was] forming locusts at [the] beginning of the coming up of the late crop; and look, [it was the] late crop after the mowings of the king.
pieces: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was forming swarms of locusts just as the late crop was beginning to come up, the crop that grows after the king's share has been mown.

L.1: Thus the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was forming locusts at the beginning of the coming up of the late crop; and look, [it was] the late crop after the king's mowings.

R.1: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me a vision. He was making swarms of locusts. It was just when the second crop was starting to come up, after the king's share of the first crop had been cut.

decisions.choice: the first of five visions
decisions.reason: Chapters 7-9 report five visions: the locusts (7:1-3), the fire (7:4-6), the plumb line (7:7-9), the basket of summer fruit (8:1-3) and the Lord beside the altar (9:1-4). The first four begin the same way, 'Thus the Lord GOD showed me'. In the first two Amos prays and the LORD relents; in the next two the LORD says that he will no longer pass by his people; in the last there is no dialogue at all. Amos tells the visions in prose, with his words and the LORD's as a conversation.

decisions.choice: the late crop after the king's mowings: the second growth of spring, after the king's share was cut
decisions.reason: Leqesh is the late growth that comes up with the spring rains. 'The king's mowings' seem to be a first cutting taken as tax, perhaps for the royal horses and herds (compare 1 Kings 18:5). The late crop was what the farmers had left for themselves and their animals; if locusts ate it, there would be nothing until the next year.

decisions.choice: locusts: swarms of locusts
decisions.reason: Gobay is a word for locusts (Nahum 3:17). A swarm could strip a land bare (Joel 1:4). The LORD is 'forming' them, the word used of a potter shaping clay: the plague is his work.

decisions.choice: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: look (L); This is what the Lord GOD showed me (B); The Lord GOD showed me a vision (R)
decisions.reason: The opening formula of the visions keeps one wording at each level in 7:1, 4, 7 and 8:1. 'Look' (hinneh) is kept at Literal and left to the sense at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: swarms of; the crop that grows after (B); the second crop; of the first crop (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain what the late crop and the king's mowings were (m2).

records.heading: Locusts and fire

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־כִּלָּה֙ לֶֽאֱכוֹל֙ אֶת־עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֔רֶץ וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ סְֽלַֽח־נָ֔א מִ֥י יָק֖וּם יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב כִּ֥י קָטֹ֖ן הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And it was, when it had finished eating the vegetation of the land, I said, Lord Yahweh, forgive, please! How will Jacob stand? For he [is] small.
pieces: When they had eaten up the green plants of the land, I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please forgive! How can Jacob survive? He is so small."

L.2: And it happened, when they had finished eating the vegetation of the land, that I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, forgive, please! How can Jacob stand? For he [is] small."

R.2: The locusts ate every green plant in the land. Then I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please forgive your people! How can Israel survive? It is so small and weak."

decisions.choice: when they had finished eating: Amos prays as the locusts finish their work
alternatives: if they finished eating (a warning before it happens)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew 'and it was, if they finished' is unusual. It is usually read as 'when they had finished'. In the vision Amos sees the crop all but gone, and he prays before the picture becomes fact.

decisions.choice: forgive: pardon the people's sin, and so hold back the judgment
decisions.reason: Amos does not deny that the people deserve judgment; he asks the LORD to pardon them. In the second vision he asks only that the LORD stop (verse 5).

decisions.choice: How can Jacob stand? He is small: Israel is too weak to survive such a blow
decisions.reason: Amos calls the people 'Jacob', the name of their ancestor, and pleads that they are small and helpless. The rich of Samaria thought themselves 'the first of the nations' (6:1); the prophet sees how small they are before the LORD.

decisions.choice: survive (B, R); Israel; your people; small and weak (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'survive' for 'stand'. Readable says 'Israel' for 'Jacob', adds 'your people' as the object of 'forgive', and adds 'weak' to bring out what 'small' means here (m3).

records.source: נִחַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַל־זֹ֑את לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Yahweh relented concerning this. It will not be, said Yahweh.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented. "It will not happen," {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said.

L.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning this. "It will not happen," said {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.3: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} changed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind. "It will not happen," said {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: relented: the LORD turned back from the judgment he had shown
decisions.reason: Nicham means to be sorry or to change one's course. It is often used of the LORD holding back a punishment he had announced (Exodus 32:14; Jeremiah 18:8; Jonah 3:10). It shows that the prophet's prayer mattered. It does not mean that the LORD had done wrong.

decisions.choice: changed his mind (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says 'changed his mind' for 'relented', in the sense explained in m1.

records.source: כֹּ֤ה הִרְאַ֨נִי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה קֹרֵ֛א לָרִ֥ב בָּאֵ֖שׁ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וַתֹּ֨אכַל֙ אֶת־תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וְאָכְלָ֖ה אֶת־הַחֵֽלֶק׃
records.gloss: Thus showed me [the] Lord Yahweh, and look, [the] Lord Yahweh [was] calling to contend by fire; and it devoured the great deep, and it was devouring the portion.
pieces: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: there was the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, summoning fire to judge. It dried up the great deep and was eating up the land.

L.4: Thus the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me: look, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} was calling to contend by fire, and it devoured the great deep and was devouring the portion [of land].

R.4: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} showed me another vision. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} was calling for fire to punish the people. The fire dried up the deep waters under the earth and began to burn up the land.

decisions.choice: calling to contend by fire: summoning fire to carry out his case against Israel
alternatives: calling for a rain of fire (dividing the letters as lirvivei 'esh)
decisions.reason: Riv is a legal case, and the LORD calls for fire to carry out his judgment (compare Isaiah 66:16). The phrase 'to contend by fire' is unusual, and some divide the letters differently to read 'calling for a shower of fire'. The sense is close either way: a fire of judgment sent by the LORD.

decisions.choice: the great deep: the waters under the earth that feed springs and rivers
decisions.reason: Tehom rabbah is the great deep, the waters below the earth (Genesis 7:11; Isaiah 51:10). This fire is so fierce that it dries up the sources of water, and then it begins on the land.

decisions.choice: the portion: the land given to Israel as its share
decisions.reason: Cheleq is a share or allotted portion, here the farmland divided among Israel's families (Micah 2:4). The fire is eating up the land itself.

decisions.choice: summoning fire to judge (B); to punish the people (R); dried up; the land (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'the land' for 'the portion' (m3) and 'dried up' for what fire does to water. Readable explains 'the great deep' (m2) and says what the fire is for.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ חֲדַל־נָ֔א מִ֥י יָק֖וּם יַעֲקֹ֑ב כִּ֥י קָטֹ֖ן הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And I said, Lord Yahweh, cease, please! How will Jacob stand? For he [is] small.
pieces: Then I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please stop! How can Jacob survive? He is so small."

L.5: And I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, cease, please! How can Jacob stand? For he [is] small."

R.5: Then I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, please stop! How can Israel survive? It is so small and weak."

decisions.choice: cease: Amos now asks only that the LORD hold back
decisions.reason: In verse 2 Amos asked the LORD to forgive; now he asks only that he stop. The rest of the plea repeats verse 2 word for word, and the wording here repeats it at each level.

records.source: נִחַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַל־זֹ֑את גַּם־הִיא֙ לֹ֣א תִֽהְיֶ֔ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Yahweh relented concerning this. Also it will not be, said [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented. "This will not happen either," the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} said.

L.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning this. "This also will not happen," said the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.6: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} changed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind again. "This will not happen either," said the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the LORD relents again, as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The LORD answers as in verse 3, now with 'also'. Twice the prophet's prayer holds back judgment. In the next two visions he does not pray, and the LORD says that he will not pass by his people again (7:8; 8:2).

records.source: כֹּ֣ה הִרְאַ֔נִי וְהִנֵּ֧ה אֲדֹנָ֛י נִצָּ֖ב עַל־חוֹמַ֣ת אֲנָ֑ךְ וּבְיָד֖וֹ אֲנָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Thus he showed me, and look, [the] Lord [was] standing on a wall of plumb line, and in his hand a plumb line.
pieces: This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed me: the Lord was standing beside a wall built true to a plumb line, with a plumb line in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand.

L.7: Thus {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed me: look, the Lord was standing beside a wall [built with] a plumb line, with a plumb line in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand.

R.7: Then the Lord showed me another vision. He was standing beside a wall that had been built straight, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was holding a plumb line.

decisions.choice: 'anakh: a plumb line, a weight of lead or tin hung on a cord
alternatives: tin: a wall of tin, and tin in his hand
decisions.reason: The word 'anakh is found only in verses 7-8. It has long been understood as a plumb line, a weight hung on a cord to test whether a wall is straight. In Akkadian, a related language, the word means tin, and some take the vision to show the Lord holding tin: perhaps a picture of weapons, or of a wall that cannot stand, or a play on a word for groaning. The plumb line fits verse 8 best: the LORD will test his people as a builder tests a wall, and a crooked wall comes down (compare 2 Kings 21:13; Isaiah 28:17).

decisions.choice: the Lord was standing: Amos sees the Lord himself in this vision
decisions.reason: In the first two visions Amos was shown what the Lord was doing; here he sees the Lord himself, standing beside the wall. The usual words 'the Lord GOD' are shortened to 'he' and 'the Lord'.

decisions.choice: built true to a plumb line (B); built straight (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what 'a wall of a plumb line' means: a wall built straight, checked with a plumb line (m1). Readable names the Lord at the start, since 'he' alone would be unclear.

records.heading: The plumb line

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י מָֽה־אַתָּ֤ה רֹאֶה֙ עָמ֔וֹס וָאֹמַ֖ר אֲנָ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י הִנְנִ֨י שָׂ֤ם אֲנָךְ֙ בְּקֶ֨רֶב֙ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹֽא־אוֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד עֲב֥וֹר לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh said to me, What [are] you seeing, Amos? And I said, A plumb line. And [the] Lord said, Look, I [am] setting a plumb line in [the] midst of my people Israel; I will not again pass by him anymore.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} asked me, "What do you see, Amos?" I answered, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Look, I am placing a plumb line among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. I will no longer pass them by.

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A plumb line." And the Lord said, "Look, I am putting a plumb line in the midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel; never again will I pass by them.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} asked me, "Amos, what do you see?" I answered, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "I am going to test {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel with a plumb line, to see whether they are straight. I will not let them go unpunished any longer.

decisions.choice: setting a plumb line in the midst of my people: testing Israel and finding it crooked
decisions.reason: A builder holds a plumb line against a wall to see whether it is straight, and a wall that leans has to be pulled down. The LORD is testing his people by his standard, and verse 9 gives the result.

decisions.choice: I will not pass by them again: I will no longer spare them
decisions.reason: To pass by someone is to overlook their wrong and spare them (Micah 7:18; Proverbs 19:11). In the first two visions the LORD relented; now he says he will not spare them again. 8:2 repeats the line. Compare 5:17, where he will pass through their midst to judge them.

decisions.choice: test ... to see whether they are straight; let them go unpunished (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what setting a plumb line among the people means (m1) and what 'pass by' means (m2).

records.source: וְנָשַׁ֨מּוּ֙ בָּמ֣וֹת יִשְׂחָ֔ק וּמִקְדְּשֵׁ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יֶחֱרָ֑בוּ וְקַמְתִּ֛י עַל־בֵּ֥ית יָרָבְעָ֖ם בֶּחָֽרֶב׃פ
records.gloss: And will be desolate [the] high places of Isaac, and [the] sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with [the] sword.
pieces: Isaac's high places will be made desolate and Israel's sanctuaries will lie in ruins, and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."

L.9: And the high places of Isaac will be made desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel will lie in ruins, and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."

R.9: The hilltop places where Isaac's people worship will be destroyed. Israel's holy places will be left in ruins. And I will come against King Jeroboam's family with the sword."

decisions.choice: the high places of Isaac: hilltop shrines, named after Israel's ancestor Isaac
decisions.reason: Bamot were open-air shrines, often on hills. Only Amos calls Israel 'Isaac' (also verse 16). The name may point to Beersheba, which was linked with Isaac (5:5; 8:14; Genesis 26:23-25), or simply to the people as Isaac's descendants.

decisions.choice: the house of Jeroboam: the royal family of Jeroboam II
decisions.reason: Jeroboam II was king of Israel when Amos prophesied (1:1). His son Zechariah reigned only six months before he was murdered, and with him the family's rule ended (2 Kings 15:8-10).

decisions.choice: hilltop places where Isaac's people worship; King Jeroboam's family (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the high places were and who 'Isaac' is (m1), and that the house of Jeroboam is the king's family (m2).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל אֶל־יָרָבְעָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר קָשַׁ֨ר עָלֶ֜יךָ עָמ֗וֹס בְּקֶ֨רֶב֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹא־תוּכַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ לְהָכִ֖יל אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos has conspired against you in [the] midst of the house of Israel; the land is not able to bear all his words.
pieces: Amaziah the priest of Bethel then sent a message to Jeroboam king of Israel: "Amos is plotting against you in the very heart of Israel. The land cannot endure all his words.

L.10: And Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent [a message] to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, "Amos has made a conspiracy against you within the house of Israel. The land cannot bear all his words.

R.10: Amaziah, the priest at Bethel, sent a message to Jeroboam, the king of Israel. He said, "Amos is plotting against you right here among the people of Israel. The country cannot put up with all the things he is saying.

decisions.choice: a story set among the visions
decisions.reason: Verses 10-17 tell, in prose, how the priest of Bethel tried to silence Amos. The story follows the third vision because that vision ends with the sword against the house of Jeroboam (verse 9), the words Amaziah reports to the king (verse 11). It is the only story about Amos in the book, and it speaks of him in the third person.

decisions.choice: Amaziah the priest of Bethel: the chief priest of the royal shrine
decisions.reason: Bethel was the king's sanctuary (verse 13), set up by Jeroboam I (1 Kings 12:28-33). Amaziah is known only from this passage.

decisions.choice: conspired: plotted rebellion; the land cannot bear his words
decisions.reason: Qashar is the word for a political plot against a king (2 Kings 15:10). Amaziah presents Amos's words as treason. The land 'cannot bear' them, as a vessel cannot hold more than it can contain.

records.heading: Amos and Amaziah

records.source: כִּי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר עָמ֔וֹס בַּחֶ֖רֶב יָמ֣וּת יָרָבְעָ֑ם וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל גָּלֹ֥ה יִגְלֶ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: For thus has said Amos: By the sword Jeroboam will die, and Israel will surely go into exile from upon its land.
pieces: For this is what Amos is saying: 'Jeroboam is going to die by the sword, and Israel will certainly be exiled, away from its land.'"

L.11: For thus Amos has said: 'By the sword Jeroboam will die, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"

R.11: Amos is saying, 'Jeroboam will be killed by the sword, and the people of Israel will surely be taken from their land as captives.'"

decisions.choice: Jeroboam will die by the sword: Amaziah sharpens verse 9
decisions.reason: Amos had said that the LORD would rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword (verse 9), not that Jeroboam himself would die by it. Amaziah leaves the LORD out and makes the words sharper. 2 Kings 14:29 says that Jeroboam II died and was buried with his ancestors; it was his son Zechariah who was killed (2 Kings 15:10).

decisions.choice: will surely go into exile: be taken away as captives
decisions.reason: The words repeat Amos's warnings (5:5, 27). In verse 17 Amos says them again, word for word.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲמַצְיָה֙ אֶל־עָמ֔וֹס חֹזֶ֕ה לֵ֥ךְ בְּרַח־לְךָ֖ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה וֶאֱכָל־שָׁ֣ם לֶ֔חֶם וְשָׁ֖ם תִּנָּבֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And Amaziah said to Amos, Seer, go, flee for yourself to the land of Judah, and eat there bread, and there you may prophesy.
pieces: Then Amaziah said to Amos, "Go away, you seer! Run off to the land of Judah. Make your living there, and do your prophesying there.

L.12: And Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer, go, flee away to the land of Judah, and eat bread there, and prophesy there.

R.12: Then Amaziah said to Amos, "Get out of here, you prophet! Go back to the land of Judah. Earn your living there by prophesying.

decisions.choice: seer: a prophet, perhaps said with scorn
decisions.reason: Chozeh, 'one who sees visions', was an honored title (2 Samuel 24:11). On Amaziah's lips it may be scornful, since Amos has just told his visions.

decisions.choice: eat bread there: make your living there
decisions.reason: Amaziah assumes that Amos prophesies for pay, as professional prophets did (Micah 3:5, 11), and tells him to go and earn it in his own country. Amos came from Tekoa in Judah (1:1).

decisions.choice: you prophet; Go back; Earn your living there by prophesying (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says 'prophet' for 'seer', 'go back' for 'flee', since Amos came from Judah, and joins the last two commands to show what Amaziah means (m2).

records.source: וּבֵֽית־אֵ֔ל לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד לְהִנָּבֵ֑א כִּ֤י מִקְדַּשׁ־מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ ה֔וּא וּבֵ֥ית מַמְלָכָ֖ה הֽוּא׃ס
records.gloss: But [at] Bethel do not again prophesy anymore, for a sanctuary of a king it [is], and a house of a kingdom it [is].
pieces: But never prophesy again at Bethel, for it is the king's sanctuary and a royal temple."

L.13: But at Bethel do not prophesy again anymore, for it [is] the king's sanctuary, and it [is] a house of the kingdom."

R.13: But never prophesy here at Bethel again. This is where the king worships. It is the temple of the kingdom."

decisions.choice: a house of the kingdom: a royal or national temple
decisions.reason: Bayit can be a palace or a temple. Beside 'the king's sanctuary', it means the kingdom's chief temple, under the king's protection. Amaziah answers to the king; he says nothing of the LORD.

decisions.choice: a royal temple (B); the temple of the kingdom (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'temple' for 'house', since the sense is a sanctuary (m1).

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַן עָמוֹס֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־אֲמַצְיָ֔ה לֹא־נָבִ֣יא אָנֹ֔כִי וְלֹ֥א בֶן־נָבִ֖יא אָנֹ֑כִי כִּֽי־בוֹקֵ֥ר אָנֹ֖כִי וּבוֹלֵ֥ס שִׁקְמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And Amos answered and said to Amaziah, Not a prophet [am] I, and not a son of a prophet [am] I; for a herdsman [am] I, and a dresser of sycamore figs.
pieces: Amos answered Amaziah, "I am not a prophet, nor a member of a company of prophets. I am a herdsman, and I take care of sycamore-fig trees.

L.14: And Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I [am] not a prophet, and I [am] not a son of a prophet; but I [am] a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs.

R.14: Amos answered Amaziah, "I am not a prophet, and I was not trained as a prophet. I raise livestock, and I take care of fig trees.

decisions.choice: I am not a prophet, nor a prophet's son: Amos denies being a professional prophet
alternatives: I was not a prophet, nor a prophet's son (until the LORD called me)
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses no verb here, so the sentence can be read in the present ('I am not') or the past ('I was not'). In the present, Amos refuses Amaziah's picture of him as a prophet who earns his bread by prophesying (verse 12): he is not one of the professionals. In the past, he means that he was not a prophet until the LORD took him from the flock (verse 15). Either way, he prophesies because the LORD sent him, not because it is his trade; in verse 15 the LORD himself tells him to 'prophesy'.

decisions.choice: a son of a prophet: a member of a company of prophets
decisions.reason: 'Sons of the prophets' were groups of prophets who lived and worked together, often under a leader such as Elisha (2 Kings 2:3; 4:38). 'Son' here means a member or disciple, not a child. Amos says that he never belonged to such a group.

decisions.choice: a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs
decisions.reason: Boqer is one who keeps cattle (baqar). In 1:1 Amos is called one of the sheep breeders of Tekoa, and in verse 15 the LORD took him 'from following the flock'. The sycamore fig is a kind of fig tree that grew in the warm lowlands (1 Kings 10:27). Its fruit had to be slit or pinched while growing so that it would ripen and be sweet, and boles seems to name that work. Amos may have owned flocks and orchards or worked for others; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: a member of a company of prophets (B); trained as a prophet; raise livestock; fig trees (R)
decisions.reason: Ben-navi' is 'a son of a prophet' at Literal, 'a member of a company of prophets' at Balanced and 'trained as a prophet' at Readable, as 2 Kings 2:3 and the terms note settle (m2). Readable says 'I was not trained' for the present 'I am not a son of a prophet', which comes to the same thing. It says 'raise livestock' for 'herdsman' and 'fig trees' for 'sycamore figs'.

records.source: וַיִּקָּחֵ֣נִי יְהוָ֔ה מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י הַצֹּ֑אן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ יְהוָ֔ה לֵ֥ךְ הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל־עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh took me from after the flock, and Yahweh said to me, Go, prophesy to my people Israel.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took me from tending the flock and told me, 'Go and prophesy to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'

L.15: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took me from following the flock, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Go, prophesy to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'

R.15: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took me away from taking care of the sheep. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told me, 'Go and prophesy to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'

decisions.choice: took me from following the flock: as the LORD took David
decisions.reason: The LORD says of David, 'I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep' (2 Samuel 7:8; compare Psalm 78:70-71). Amos's authority does not come from a group of prophets or from a shrine, but from the LORD's call.

decisions.choice: my people Israel: the LORD still calls them his people
decisions.reason: Even when he sends Amos with words of judgment, the LORD calls Israel 'my people' (7:8; 8:2).

records.source: וְעַתָּ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֗ר לֹ֤א תִנָּבֵא֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹ֥א תַטִּ֖יף עַל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂחָֽק׃
records.gloss: And now hear the word of Yahweh. You [are] saying, You shall not prophesy against Israel, and you shall not drip against the house of Isaac.
pieces: So now hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You tell me, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and stop preaching against the house of Isaac.'

L.16: And now hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You are saying, 'You shall not prophesy against Israel, and you shall not drip [words] against the house of Isaac.'

R.16: Now listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. You tell me, 'Do not prophesy against Israel. Stop preaching against the people of Isaac.'

decisions.choice: drip words: preach, let words fall like drops
decisions.reason: Hittif, 'to drip', is used of speaking or preaching (Micah 2:6, 11; Ezekiel 21:2). It may carry a note of scorn, like 'drivel'.

decisions.choice: you say: Amos quotes Amaziah's order back to him
decisions.reason: Amaziah's words of verse 13 are given again in a sharper form, now as the very thing for which judgment will come. Israel and the house of Isaac are the same people (verse 9).

decisions.choice: preaching (B, R); the people of Isaac (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1). Readable says 'people' for 'house'.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֞ בָּעִ֤יר תִּזְנֶה֙ וּבָנֶ֤יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ וְאַדְמָתְךָ֖ בַּחֶ֣בֶל תְּחֻלָּ֑ק וְאַתָּ֗ה עַל־אֲדָמָ֤ה טְמֵאָה֙ תָּמ֔וּת וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל גָּלֹ֥ה יִגְלֶ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: Your wife in the city will be a prostitute, and your sons and your daughters by the sword will fall, and your land by a measuring line will be divided, and you on unclean ground will die, and Israel will surely go into exile from upon its land.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'Your wife will be made a prostitute in the city, your sons and daughters will be struck down by the sword, and your land will be measured out and divided. You yourself will die in an unclean land, and Israel will surely go into exile, away from its land.'"

L.17: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Your wife in the city will be a prostitute, and your sons and your daughters by the sword will fall, and your land will be divided up by measuring line; and you yourself will die on unclean ground, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"

R.17: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'Your wife will have to become a prostitute in the city. Your sons and daughters will be killed by the sword. Your land will be measured and divided up among others. You yourself will die in a foreign land, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is not worshiped. And the people of Israel will surely be taken from their land as captives.'"

decisions.choice: the fate of a conquered city
decisions.reason: Each line names what happened when a city fell: women were taken by the soldiers or left to support themselves by prostitution, the young were killed, and the land was measured out for new owners (Micah 2:4-5). Amaziah himself would die in exile.

decisions.choice: unclean ground: a foreign land
decisions.reason: Israel's land belonged to the LORD. Any other land was unclean, because other gods were worshiped there and its food was not dedicated to the LORD (Hosea 9:3-4; Ezekiel 4:13). A priest, whose life was bound up with what is clean and unclean, would die in such a place.

decisions.choice: Israel will surely go into exile: Amos repeats the words Amaziah reported
decisions.reason: Amos does not take back the words Amaziah complained of (verse 11); he repeats them word for word, as the LORD's sentence.

decisions.choice: be a prostitute (L); be made a prostitute (B); have to become a prostitute (R)
decisions.reason: Here zanah is used of real prostitution, not of Israel's unfaithfulness to God, so the wording settled for Hosea ('prostitute oneself', 'be unfaithful') is not used. Balanced says 'be made' and Readable 'have to', since in a conquered city it would be forced on her (m1).

decisions.choice: among others; a foreign land, where the LORD is not worshiped (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who will get the land (m1) and what 'unclean ground' means (m2).
